answer.rationale: The degradation timeline is tightly correlated with the release 2 hours ago: p99 latency climbing for 90 minutes, release deployed 2 hours ago. This is the strongest signal. Memory_b1 establishes that rollback is a reliable tool in this organization and clears checkout errors decisively without customer impact. Memory_b2 confirms regional failover works but takes traffic shifting; here we have a single-region problem and heavy settlement load at peak—moving traffic risks cascading issues. The write path is under stress and we cannot afford coordination delays. Rollback is fastest, most contained, and removes the variable introduced to the system. We verify b1 (successful rollback precedent) and b2 (failover as viable backup if rollback reveals a deeper issue). Other options (capacity, circuit breaker, read replica routing) do not address a corrupted release and leave the bad build in the hot path.
